title: Neomorphism vs Claymorphism
lede: Both shape elements with a paired light and dark shadow instead of borders. The difference is whether the element is carved out of the background or resting on top of it.
verdict: Neumorphism carves: the element is the same colour as the surface, and the shadow pair is what makes it appear raised or pressed. Claymorphism colours: each card has its own pastel fill, a 26px radius, and a shadow pair that sits entirely outside it.
brief: The shared technique is easy to miss. Both styles refuse borders and gradients, and both build depth from two shadows — a light one from one direction and a dark one from the other. That is why they get lumped together.

What separates them is the relationship to the background. A neumorphic card is the same colour as the page, so it has no edge of its own; the only thing separating it from the surface is the shadow. A clay card is a different colour from the page, so it has a clear silhouette before any shadow is applied — and because it sits on the surface rather than being cut into it, hovering can lift it 4px without breaking the illusion.

whenA: The interface is sparse and the surface is a single colour throughout — a smart-home panel, a single-purpose control
You want physicality without colour: buttons that look pressable, switches that look moulded
The audience sees the same screen repeatedly and learns the shadows as affordances
whenB: Cards need to be distinguished from each other, which colour does instantly and shadow does not
The content is friendly or consumer-facing, where pastel reads as approachable rather than washed out
You need enough contrast for body copy without abandoning the soft look
promptDelta: The single sentence that decides this is whether the element shares the background colour. Say that the card is the same value as the page and the model produces neumorphism; say the card has its own tint and a 26px radius and you get clay. Both prompts should forbid borders, because a 1px line immediately breaks either effect, and both should cap the shadow blur relative to the radius or the result reads as a soft drop shadow rather than moulded material.
